correctness.rationale: For ξ_i∼Bern(λ/n), B_i∼Bern(1/2), the unthinned centered row converges to Pois(λ)−λ and the selected row to Pois(λ/2)−λ/2, with uniform integrability from bounded second moments. Telescoping yields E|Pois(t)−t|=2t P(Pois(t)=floor t). On each integer interval d² log R/dλ²=(floor λ−floor(λ/2))/λ²≥0, hence maxima at integers. Robbins Stirling inequalities strictly bound all even integers and odd ≥5 below R(1)=√e/2; λ=3 is checked explicitly. Thus λ=1 uniquely maximizes over all λ>0; λ→0 gives 1/2 and λ→∞ gives 1/√2. For universal C√q centered thinning, the example enforces C≥√(e/2), with no assertion of attaining the universal constant. Independently tested 4800 Poisson ratios/interval samples.
residual_risks: No uniform-in-λ finite-n convergence claimed; restriction q=1/2 and iid sparse bounded centered examples is essential.
